items.title: FarEye helps reduce e-commerce major Flipkart logistics expenses by 6%
items.rss_summary: AI-powered enterprise SaaS Far Eye on Sunday said it has helped e-commerce major Flipkart's B2B cash-and-carry market place, Flipkart Wholesale, slash its logistics spend by 6 per cent besides an 8 per cent reduction in vehicle deployment pan-India. This has enabled Flipkart Wholesale to improve fleet productivity without compromising delivery efficiency, reducing vehicle idle time by 10 per cent, Far Eye said in a statement. The improvements come from digitising and connecting dispatch, routing, compliance and payment collection processes across a network comprising 26 stores and one cross-dock, it said. Flipkart Wholesale's network processes more than 200,000 orders and about 195,000 vehicle assignments a month. The platform said it now supports the movement of goods across this network through a unified digital workflow, replacing largely manual and fragmented dispatch processes. items.title: MPCB asks Adani firm to stop work on temporary labour camp in Satara
items.rss_summary: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) has directed Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd to stop excavation and construction work for its temporary camp in Satara district for allegedly beginning these without obtaining the necessary environmental clearance and permissions. The labour camp in Satara's Patan taluka, some 300 kilometres from here, is part of the firm's 1500 MW Tarali Pumped Storage Project. In a stop-work notice dated November 20, the MPCB said the company had started excavation and development work at Gat Nos. 33 and 34 in Sawargahar village for a temporary labour camp and other storage activities without informing the board or obtaining the required permissions. The company had not secured environmental clearance for the excavation and development work from the competent authority, the MPCB added. The notice, issued under Section 33A of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974, and Section 31A of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act .

items.title: ITC extends Braille-enabled packaging to Fiama, takes total to 16 SKUs
items.rss_summary: Alongside an industry-wide shift toward AI-enabled personalisation and algorithmic optimisation, diversified conglomerate ITC Ltd is pursuing an analogue, inclusive approach to product innovation by incorporating raised Braille text on select personal care items from its Savlon and Fiama portfolios. The initiative makes everyday consumer products more accessible to millions of visually impaired people in India, for whom routine activities such as identifying a handwash bottle or choosing the right personal care product can pose challenges. Building on Savlon's introduction of India's first Braille-enabled FMCG packaging in 2018, ITC's Personal Care Products Business has now extended the initiative to Fiama. It now has 16 SKUs from the personal care segment under accessible packaging. Braille identifiers are currently featured on technically feasible product packs, such as Savlon Antiseptic Disinfectant Liquid, Savlon Wet Wipes and Handwash Pumps, as well as Fiama Shower Gels. items.title: Shree Cement to cross 100 MT capacity in 3-4 yrs, targets 9-10% growth
items.rss_summary: Shree Cement, the country's third-largest cement maker by installed capacity, is expecting to cross the 100 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) production capacity over the next three to four years, driven by an aggressive expansion push and steady demand from the country's infrastructure and housing sectors, said its Chairman Hari Mohan Bangur. In an interaction with PTI, Bangur said the company is targeting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9-10 per cent over the next six to seven years, higher than the expected 7-8 per cent growth in the overall Indian cement industry. Shree Cement Ltd (SCL), which earlier this month announced a Rs 7,000 crore investment to set up cement plants in Andhra Pradesh as part of its expansion, expects to reach 80 MTPA capacity in the next two years, he said. items.title: InvIT IPO rush gathers pace, 4-5 trusts likely to go public by Mar 2027
items.rss_summary: Four to five privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) are expected to tap the public markets by March 2027 to raise a combined Rs 17,000 crore, as infrastructure developers increasingly turn to this route to mobilise long-term capital and monetise operational assets, investment bankers said. InvITs have already mobilised around Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25, indicating growing investor appetite for infrastructure-backed investment opportunities, according to the Bharat InvITs Association. Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT. items.title: Airbnb looks beyond traditional holiday hubs to deepen presence in India
items.rss_summary: Global hospitality platform Airbnb is looking to deepen its presence in India by expanding beyond traditional holiday destinations, strengthening the homestay ecosystem and bringing more local entrepreneurs onto its platform to tap the country's growing domestic travel market. In an interview with PTI, Airbnb India Country Manager Amanpreet Bajaj said the company's India growth strategy will focus on expanding quality accommodation supply, enabling more communities to participate in tourism and diversifying its offerings beyond stays through experiences and services. "We will also continue expanding quality supply, both in traditional leisure markets and metros and in emerging destinations such as spiritual corridors and nature-led locations. We want travellers to have more choices and local communities to benefit from tourism," Bajaj shared. He highlighted that India is one of Airbnb's fastest-growing origin markets globally, with domestic travel emerging as a major growth driver.

items.title: EV brand E-Went eyes mass market, to test sodium-ion batteries from Dec
items.rss_summary: Kolkata-based Saraogi E-Ventures, which markets electric two-wheelers under the E-Went brand, sees significant growth opportunities in India's price-sensitive markets, particularly in the sub-Rs 1 lakh segment, while exploring sodium-ion battery technology as an alternative to conventional lithium-ion batteries, its founder and CEO Umang Kumar Saraogi said. The company plans to begin trials of sodium-ion battery-powered scooters around December, deploying some vehicles for testing. The technology is being explored for its potential safety advantages over conventional lithium-ion batteries, although its relatively lower energy density makes the battery packs bulkier, Saraogi said. "It is supposed to be safer. We expect to conduct trials here starting in December and deploy some vehicles with these batteries. The economics and convenience have to be evaluated before we can deploy them in our new product launches. Currently, most of the models use lithium-ion technology," he told PTI.

items.title: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility eyes IPO in 18 months to fund next growth phase
